nar.text: After only half an hour the cars lined up on the grid for the Final, with the sun shining through the drizzle. 11 Grand Prix cars and 6 Voiturettes qualified to start in the Final over 30 laps.
Rain tyres are allowed for the Final; Auto Union fits 22-inch wheels only to Stuck and Nuvolari, so Müller and Hasse start on 19-inch wheels.
Lang took the immediate lead just ahead of Brauchitsch and Caracciola with Farina's red Alfa lined up right behind Lang.
Müller's engine had not started when the flag fell and three mechanics helped him on the grid. The field was already out of sight when at last it fired up.
Müller stepped on the accelerator so hard that the car spun around twice on the slippery cobbled pavement. Graffenried's car also started a few seconds late.
